items.prompt: Which river valley was home to the ancient Egyptian civilization?

options.label: The Indus
The Nile
The Yellow River
The Tigris

rubric: Ancient Egypt grew along the Nile.
The Tigris, Indus and Yellow River supported Mesopotamia, Harappa and early China.

items.prompt: Which empire was ruled from the city of Rome and later controlled most of the Mediterranean coast?

options.label: The Persian Empire
The Mongol Empire
The Roman Empire
The Ottoman Empire

rubric: Rome was the capital of the Roman Empire.
Other empires had different centers and eras.

items.prompt: In what year did Christopher Columbus first reach the Americas on his voyage sponsored by Spain?
rubric: Columbus's first voyage was in 1492.
Other dates mark the Norman conquest, US independence and the Spanish Armada.

items.prompt: What name is given to the period of rapid growth of machine-based manufacturing that began in Britain in the 1700s?

options.label: The Reformation
The Industrial Revolution
The Scientific Revolution
The Agricultural Revolution

rubric: Britain began industrialization in the 1700s.
The Neolithic Revolution was farming's start; the Renaissance and Reformation were cultural and religious movements.

items.prompt: Which war was fought from 1939 to 1945 and involved the Allied and Axis powers?

options.label: The Cold War
The Crimean War
World War I
World War II

rubric: World War II ran 1939-1945.
World War I was 1914-1918; the Cold War was not a direct global war.

items.prompt: Which of the following were early river-valley civilizations? Select all that apply.

options.label: The Aztec Empire
Mesopotamia
Ancient Egypt
The Inca Empire

rubric: Mesopotamia and Egypt arose in river valleys thousands of years ago.
Aztec and Inca empires were much later and in the Americas.

items.prompt: A student is preparing a timeline of the ancient world. She needs to recall which culture invented cuneiform, one of the earliest writing systems, on clay tablets. Which culture should she label?

options.label: The Romans
The Sumerians
The Maya
The Vikings

rubric: Sumerians in Mesopotamia created cuneiform.
Romans used Latin script; Vikings used runes; the Maya used glyphs.

items.prompt: Why did early farming settlements often grow into cities?

options.label: Writing had to be invented before any farming
Cities were needed to hold the first armies
Food surpluses let some people specialize in other work
Farmers were forbidden from living in the countryside

rubric: Surplus food supported specialists and larger populations.
Other options reverse or invent causes.

items.prompt: What was the main purpose of the Silk Road trade routes?

options.label: Keeping cultures separated by controlling borders
Connecting Africa to the Americas by sea
Carrying silk from China to a single royal court in Rome
Linking Asia and Europe so goods and ideas could travel

rubric: The Silk Road connected Eurasian regions for trade and exchange.
Distractors narrow, misplace or reverse its function.

items.prompt: What best explains why the printing press with movable type, in use in Europe from the 1400s, changed society?

options.label: It gave rulers tighter control, since only royal workshops could print
It made books cheaper, so ideas spread to more people
It replaced Latin with one language, so all Europeans could read
It improved ship navigation, so Europeans reached new lands

rubric: Cheap printing widened access to texts and ideas.
Other options are false or unrelated.

items.prompt: Which statement best describes the Columbian Exchange?

options.label: Plants, animals and diseases moved between the Americas and the Old World
Gold and silver flowed from the Americas to Spain, driving a new European trade economy
Europeans and Asians traded spices, silk and porcelain along new Atlantic sea routes
A treaty divided newly claimed lands between Spain and Portugal after Columbus's voyages

rubric: It was a broad biological and cultural transfer.
Distractors reduce it to one good, wrongly place it, or call it a treaty.

items.prompt: Why is the year 1789 important in world history?

options.label: The French Revolution began, challenging monarchy and privilege
The Industrial Revolution ended as steam power gave way to electricity
The Western Roman Empire collapsed after repeated barbarian invasions
World War I began after the assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand

rubric: The French Revolution began in 1789.
Other options are events from different times.

items.prompt: Which statements correctly describe why empires expanded? Select all that apply.

options.label: Empires grew because they were forbidden to trade
Empires expanded only by peaceful agreement
Rulers wanted more land and power
Rulers sought resources and trade wealth

rubric: Wealth and power motivated expansion.
The others contradict how empires usually grew.

items.prompt: A teacher shows a source written in 1850 by a British factory owner praising factory work. A student asks whether it shows how all workers felt. What is the best explanation?

options.label: Yes, because a source written during the 1800s by someone alive then is reliable
No, it reflects one owner's view and may leave out workers' views
No, because a source written by an owner is biased and so useless to historians
Yes, because factory owners saw the workers daily and knew them best

rubric: Sources reflect the author's perspective, so other voices are needed.
Distractors treat age or position as proof, or reject sources altogether.

items.prompt: What was the main change brought by the Neolithic (Agricultural) Revolution?

options.label: People adopted iron tools first, which allowed armies to conquer and tax neighboring farmland
People shifted from farming to hunting, which allowed larger migrations and shared herds
People shifted from foraging to farming, which allowed settled villages and food surpluses
People invented writing first, which allowed rulers to organize farms across large regions

rubric: Farming allowed settlement and surplus, the base of later cities.
Distractors reverse the shift or credit later developments (iron, writing) as the cause.

items.prompt: Which statement best explains how the Silk Roads affected Eurasian societies?

options.label: They linked distant regions, so goods, technologies and religions such as Buddhism spread
They were mainly military supply routes, so cultural exchange happened largely through conquest
They mostly carried luxury goods for elites, so ordinary people met few outside ideas or crafts
They were controlled by one imperial government, so laws and languages became fairly uniform

rubric: The Silk Roads were networks of exchange that spread goods, technology and religion.
Distractors claim political unity, no cultural effect, or military-only use.

items.prompt: What does the term Pax Romana describe?

options.label: A treaty with Persia that divided the Roman Empire into eastern and western halves
A period when the Senate ruled without emperors, which reduced the role of the army
A religious reform that made Christianity the only legal faith in every Roman province
A long period of relative peace and stability within the empire that helped trade flourish

rubric: Pax Romana means roughly two centuries of stability beginning under Augustus.
Distractors confuse it with the later division, Christian legalization or the Republic.

items.prompt: Which pair of crops originated in the Americas and later spread to Europe and Asia through the Columbian Exchange?

options.label: Horses and sugarcane
Wheat and rice
Coffee and bananas
Potatoes and maize

rubric: Potatoes and maize were American crops that spread worldwide.
The other pairs include Old World crops or animals brought to the Americas.

items.prompt: Why did the printing press with movable type help Reformation ideas spread in the 1500s?

options.label: It made pamphlets and Bibles cheap and quick to copy, so ideas reached many readers fast
It let the Church control which texts were produced, so reform ideas were officially approved
It was banned in Protestant lands, so ideas travelled mainly through handwritten manuscripts
It replaced Latin with one European language, so all readers could understand the same texts

rubric: Cheap, fast printing multiplied the reach of reformers' writings.
Distractors invent Church control, a single language or a ban on printing.

items.prompt: Which of the following were long-term causes of World War I? Select all that apply.

options.label: Militarism and an arms race among the major European powers
The punitive Treaty of Versailles of 1919
A system of rival alliances that pulled many states into one conflict
Nationalist tensions, especially in the Balkans
The Great Depression of the 1930s

rubric: Alliances, militarism and nationalism built tension before 1914.
Versailles and the Depression came after the war began or ended.

items.prompt: A student reads that in 1324 Mansa Musa of Mali made a pilgrimage to Mecca, giving away so much gold that prices in Cairo were affected. Later European maps showed him holding a gold nugget. What does this best show about Mali?

options.label: Mali was a wealthy West African state connected to trans-Saharan and Islamic world networks
Mali's wealth came mainly from Atlantic slave trading with Europeans before 1324
Mali was isolated from other regions until Europeans arrived in the fifteenth century
Mali was a minor kingdom whose ruler travelled abroad to seek aid against invaders

rubric: The pilgrimage and the gold show Mali's wealth and its links to wider trade and Islamic networks.
Distractors assume isolation, a wrong date and source of wealth, or a mistaken purpose.

items.prompt: A trade ledger from about 1600 lists Chinese porcelain, Indian cotton and Spanish silver from the Americas, all sold at Manila. Which trade network does it show?

options.label: The Viking river routes to Constantinople
The Atlantic triangular trade linking only Europe, Africa and the Americas
The Manila galleon trade linking Asia and the Americas
The trans-Saharan gold and salt trade

rubric: Manila was the hub connecting Asian goods with American silver.
Other options are real networks but do not match the goods and place.

items.prompt: In 1830 a country has abundant coal and iron, growing capital and new steam-powered textile machinery. Which outcome would you most expect over the next decades?

options.label: Wage labor disappearing as families make cloth at home again
Falling demand for coal as steam power is replaced by water wheels
Rapid growth of factory towns and urban populations
Cities shrinking as workers return to farms to escape machines

rubric: Industrialization drew workers to factory towns and increased urbanization.
Distractors reverse the trend of urbanization, wage labor and coal use.

items.prompt: A historian finds a letter written in July 1789 by a Parisian shopkeeper describing the crowds at the Bastille. How should the letter be classified?

options.label: A secondary source, because letters are never reliable evidence
A primary source, because it was written by a witness at the time
A primary source, because it was written by a government official
A secondary source, because it is about a famous event

rubric: A contemporary eyewitness account is a primary source.
Distractors confuse topic fame or reliability with source type, or invent an official author.

items.prompt: A student must explain why India (1947), Ghana (1957) and Indonesia (1949) gained independence within about a decade. Which explanation best applies?

options.label: Colonies became independent only after they had industrialized fully
Colonial powers grew richer after World War II and chose to grant freedom voluntarily
Colonial powers were weakened by World War II, while nationalist movements gained strength
The League of Nations sent armies to remove colonial governments after 1945

rubric: War-weakened empires and organised nationalist movements drove decolonization.
Distractors invent voluntary generosity, League intervention or an industrial precondition.

items.prompt: The Han dynasty of China ended in 220 CE and the Western Roman Empire fell in 476 CE. How many years separate these two events?
rubric: 476 minus 220 equals 256.
Other numbers come from arithmetic slips.

items.prompt: Which of these revolutions were inspired in part by Enlightenment ideas such as natural rights and popular sovereignty? Select all that apply.

options.label: The Taiping Rebellion beginning in 1850
The Haitian Revolution beginning in 1791
The Russian Revolution beginning in 1917
The American Revolution beginning in 1775

items.prompt: A museum is writing a label for a sixteenth-century brass plaque from the Kingdom of Benin in West Africa. The plaque was among thousands of objects removed when British forces sacked Benin City in 1897. Which sentence would make the label most accurate?

options.label: Made in Egypt for a pharaoh and brought to Europe by medieval merchants trading across the Mediterranean
Made by Ottoman craftsmen for a sultan and later taken from Istanbul by British troops in 1897
Made by Edo artisans for the Oba's court and removed in the British expedition of 1897
Made in Portugal for the Africa trade and given to the Oba of Benin as a diplomatic gift in the 1500s

rubric: Benin plaques were made by Edo artisans for the Oba's court and looted in 1897.
Distractors assign wrong makers, origins or histories.

items.prompt: A historian wants to show how long-distance trade networks carried disease. Which event best applies the idea that Eurasian trade routes spread epidemics?

options.label: The 1918 influenza travelling with soldiers returning from the Western Front
Cholera spreading from the Ganges delta along British steamship lines in 1817
Smallpox reaching the Aztec capital after Spanish landings in 1519
The Black Death moving from Central Asia to Mediterranean ports in the 1340s

rubric: The Black Death followed Mongol-era overland and sea trade routes across Eurasia.
The other options are real epidemics but belong to Atlantic, imperial or wartime networks, not the Eurasian trade routes of the question.

items.prompt: Which list places these events in correct chronological order, earliest first?

options.label: Peloponnesian War, founding of the Han dynasty, Mongol sack of Baghdad, fall of Western Rome
Peloponnesian War, fall of Western Rome, founding of the Han dynasty, Mongol sack of Baghdad
Founding of the Han dynasty, Peloponnesian War, fall of Western Rome, Mongol sack of Baghdad
Peloponnesian War, founding of the Han dynasty, fall of Western Rome, Mongol sack of Baghdad

rubric: Dates run: Peloponnesian War (431 BCE), Han founded (206 BCE), Western Rome falls (476 CE), Baghdad sacked (1258).
Distractors swap Greek and Chinese events or place Rome's fall after the Mongols.

items.prompt: A 17th-century European state follows mercantilist policy toward its colonies. Which action would that state most likely take?

options.label: Accept a trade deficit with colonies to keep consumer prices low
Remove tariffs so colonists can sell sugar to any rival empire
Encourage colonies to build manufacturing that competes with home industry
Require colonial goods to be shipped only on its own vessels to its own ports

rubric: Mercantilism aims to keep colonial trade and bullion within the mother country, as with the English Navigation Acts.
Distractors describe free trade or colonial industrialisation, which mercantilists tried to prevent.

items.prompt: Which action best illustrates the state-led industrialisation pursued by Meiji Japan in the 1870s and 1880s?

options.label: The government shifted farmland to plantation crops sold to foreign merchants
The government left industry to samurai domains and avoided taxing agriculture
The government banned foreign advisers and relied on traditional guild artisans
The government built model factories and railways, then sold many to private firms

rubric: Meiji leaders funded pilot industries and infrastructure, later privatising many of them.
Distractors reflect isolation, colonial-style export economies, or feudal decentralisation that the Meiji state abolished.

items.prompt: Which conflict is the clearest example of a Cold War proxy war, in which the superpowers backed opposing sides without fighting each other directly?

options.label: Korean War
Russo-Japanese War
Boer War
Crimean War

rubric: In Korea, the USSR and China backed the North while the US-led UN force backed the South.
The other wars predate the Cold War.

items.prompt: Which of these were methods the Roman Empire used to integrate conquered provinces? Select all that apply.

options.label: Granting citizenship over time to provincial elites and allied communities
Letting local towns run municipal government under Roman-style law
Replacing local elites with Roman-born governors in every provincial town
Building paved roads and stationing legions that linked provinces to Rome

rubric: Roads, legions, citizenship and municipal government all tied provinces to Rome.
Christianity was not imperial policy during Rome's main expansion and was persecuted for long periods.

items.prompt: A student maps Africa in 1880 and 1914 and sees European claims expand rapidly after 1885. The student wants the rule from the Berlin Conference that explains why powers rushed to station officials and troops inland. Which principle applies?

options.label: A claim to territory was recognised only if the power effectively occupied it
Each power could claim only coastal land, leaving the interior neutral
Claims followed existing ethnic and kingdom boundaries across the continent
African rulers had to approve treaties through a council of the conference

rubric: The principle of effective occupation pushed powers to establish presence quickly to secure claims.
Distractors invent respect for African boundaries, coastal-only limits, or African approval, none of which the conference provided.

items.prompt: Spain's conquest of the Aztec Empire (1519-1521) is often attributed to guns and steel alone. Which analysis best explains the outcome?

options.label: Aztec rulers accepted Cortes's demand to convert to Christianity and gave up their capital without a prolonged fight
Spanish forces fielded far larger armies than the Aztecs, and superior numbers won the decisive battles
The Aztecs had no organised army, so they could not defend their island capital against the Spanish advance
Tlaxcalan and other Indigenous allies, plus epidemic disease, multiplied a small Spanish force

rubric: Subject peoples hostile to Aztec tribute and smallpox were decisive alongside Spanish arms.
Distractors rely on myths of an unorganised Aztec army, Spanish numerical superiority, or voluntary conversion.

items.prompt: Which factor was most clearly shared by the causes of both the French Revolution (1789) and the Russian Revolution (1917)?

options.label: A rebellion led mainly by an industrial working class
A peasant uprising that began in the provinces and then moved to the capital
Fiscal and military strain that undermined the monarchy's legitimacy
Foreign occupation of the capital by an invading army

rubric: French war debt and Russian losses in WWI both weakened trust in the crown.
Distractors apply features to the wrong case or to neither.

items.prompt: Tacitus, a Roman senator, wrote of Germanic tribes as simple, brave and honest. What is the main limit on using this as evidence of Germanic society?

options.label: He used the portrait to criticise Roman decadence and relied on secondhand reports
He wrote centuries after the events and had no access to any earlier written sources
He wrote in Latin, which cannot reliably convey Germanic customs and social terms
He was a Germanic native who exaggerated his own people's virtues to win Roman favour

rubric: Tacitus had a rhetorical purpose, contrasting Roman moral decline, and drew on others' accounts.
Distractors misstate his timing, origin or language.

items.prompt: Jews expelled from Spain in 1492 were widely received in the Ottoman Empire. Which difference between the two states best explains this?

options.label: The Ottomans let recognised religious communities govern themselves in return for taxes, while Spain sought religious uniformity
The Ottomans kept religion out of public law and treated all subjects as equal citizens, while Spain was ruled directly by the Church
The Ottomans needed Jewish soldiers for their expanding frontier armies, while Spain's crown had no use for Jewish recruits
The Ottomans shared Spain's goal of religious uniformity but lacked the administrative means to enforce it on Jews

rubric: The Ottoman millet arrangement tolerated communities under tax, while Spain's monarchs pursued uniformity.
Distractors misdescribe the Ottoman state as secular, invent military recruitment, or treat the two policies as identical.

items.prompt: Which analysis best explains how the Treaty of Versailles contributed to the rise of the Nazis?

options.label: Reparations and resentment weakened Weimar's legitimacy, and the Depression made extremism attractive
The treaty's reparations were mostly paid in full by 1923, and the resulting drain on the economy brought hyperinflation and Nazi rule
The Depression was the decisive cause of Nazi success, while the treaty's terms were largely irrelevant to German politics
The treaty left Germany's army free to rearm openly, and this military strength let the Nazis seize power by force

rubric: The treaty's burdens undermined Weimar, and the Depression provided the later trigger.
Distractors give single-cause or factually wrong accounts of payment and rearmament.

items.prompt: Which factors contributed to the collapse of China's Han dynasty around 220 CE? Select all that apply.

options.label: Powerful landowners sheltering farmland from tax, shrinking state revenue
Steppe nomad pressure on the northern frontier that cut the Silk Road trade and ended Han tax revenue
Peasant uprisings such as the Yellow Turbans that weakened central control
Provincial generals building private armies that became regional warlords

rubric: Rebellion, warlordism and a shrinking tax base all undermined the Han.
The Mongols rose roughly a thousand years later.

items.prompt: An archivist compares two accounts of the 1857 uprising in India. A British officer's memoir calls it a 'Sepoy Mutiny'; a later Indian nationalist history calls it the 'First War of Independence'. Both describe the outbreak at Meerut and the siege of Delhi. What is the best analysis of the difference?

options.label: Each label reflects the author's political aims, while the core events are shared
The nationalist account is more reliable because it was written later
The difference comes only from translation, not from the authors' views
One account must be fabricated, since honest sources cannot disagree like this

rubric: Labels carry interpretive and political purposes, while shared details show factual overlap.
Distractors assume fabrication, that later means more accurate, or that translation alone explains the gap.

items.prompt: Historians explain the collapse of Indigenous American populations after 1492 mainly by which combination of causes?

options.label: Old World diseases hit populations with no prior immunity, worsened by war, forced labour and social disruption
Deliberate European biological warfare, which spread smallpox through planned distribution of infected goods
Direct military killing by small European armies, with disease playing only a minor and later role
Famine caused by European crops displacing native agriculture, with epidemics a secondary effect

rubric: Epidemics among immunologically naive populations, amplified by conquest and labour regimes, are the accepted core explanation.
Distractors overstate warfare, famine or intentional germ warfare as the main cause.

items.prompt: Why is the Mongol Empire's 13th-14th century integration of Eurasia often linked to the spread of the Black Death?

options.label: Mongol armies carried plague directly from China to Europe as a planned weapon in every major campaign
Secure overland and steppe trade routes linked Central Asia to Black Sea ports, letting infected fleas and traders travel far
Mongol taxation caused famine across Eurasia, and malnutrition alone created the disease in new regions
The Mongols forced mass migrations of peasants into European cities, producing the crowding in which plague first arose

rubric: Connected trade routes allowed plague to move between regions along commercial corridors.
Distractors treat the Mongols as deliberate carriers or reduce plague to famine or crowding.

items.prompt: In 1923 the German government printed money to fund passive resistance to the French-Belgian occupation of the Ruhr, and hyperinflation followed. What does this sequence best show about the causes of the crisis?

options.label: The Weimar constitution's proportional voting system was the root cause, because unstable coalitions could never pass a balanced budget and so forced the state to borrow from the central bank
Reparations led to the Ruhr occupation, but the inflation came from the government's choice to finance resistance by printing money
Reparations alone caused it, because the sum demanded was so large that any German monetary policy would have ended in the same collapse of the currency
Foreign bankers caused it by withdrawing gold reserves and short-term loans from Germany, which left the government no option except to print money in reaction

rubric: The crisis chains reparations, occupation and a monetary financing decision.
Distractors collapse the chain into one factor, either reparations alone, foreign bankers or constitutional design.

items.prompt: A historian uses Hernan Cortes's letters to Charles V as evidence of how the conquest of Mexico unfolded. Which feature of the source most limits its reliability on Cortes's own role?

options.label: It was printed in Europe, and printers of that era often edited or abridged texts, so the printed wording may differ from the original
It was written years after the events, so Cortes's memory of his own decisions is likely to have faded
It was composed to justify his unauthorised expedition to the king, so he had reason to inflate his success and legitimacy
It was written in Spanish rather than Nahuatl, so it reflects only the conquerors' view of indigenous politics and warfare

rubric: Cortes wrote as a self-interested participant seeking royal approval after defying his superior.
Distractors invent problems of date, language or printing that do not apply to the letters.

items.prompt: Meiji Japan industrialised far faster after 1868 than Qing China did in the same decades. Which comparison best explains the gap?

options.label: Japan's ruling elite was more open to Western learning and sent missions abroad, while most Qing officials rejected foreign technology outright
Japan had richer coal and iron deposits near its ports, which let private firms industrialise with little help from the state
China lacked a merchant class able to finance factories, whereas Japan already had a large capitalist class by the 1860s
A centralised Meiji state sponsored reform deliberately, while Qing efforts were piecemeal, factional and strained by war indemnities

rubric: State capacity and coherence of reform account for much of the divergence.
Distractors use resource, cultural or merchant-class stereotypes that the evidence does not support.

items.prompt: Scholars analysing the Late Bronze Age collapse in the eastern Mediterranean (c. 1200 BCE) point to which interacting factors? Select all that apply.

options.label: Highly interdependent palace economies and trade networks that spread shocks
Prolonged drought and climate stress that strained agricultural surpluses
Mongol cavalry raids that cut the tin trade between Anatolia and Egypt
Invasions, migrations and internal revolts that overwhelmed weakened centres
Conquest by Roman legions that dismantled the Mycenaean and Hittite states

rubric: Climate stress, systemic interdependence and unrest or migration are the commonly cited interacting causes.
Rome and the Mongols belong to much later periods.

items.prompt: A historian reads Tang dynasty court records listing dozens of foreign envoys who 'offered tribute and submission'. Other evidence shows these envoys often carried goods for profitable exchange and returned with large gifts. What is the best inference about the records?

options.label: They show only that trade was illegal, since the missions were disguised as diplomacy to evade Tang law
They accurately show that the foreign states were political subordinates of the Tang, since the court recorded it
They are of little use, since a court source written to flatter the emperor cannot tell us about foreign contact
They reflect the court's hierarchical ideology, while the contacts also served the envoys' trade and diplomacy

rubric: Tribute language expresses court worldview, while other evidence reveals exchange motives.
Distractors take the records literally, dismiss them entirely or invent a legal explanation.

items.prompt: A student claims Britain industrialised first 'because it had coal'. Judged against the criterion that an explanation must account for why comparable coal regions did not industrialise first, which critique is strongest?

options.label: Coal mattered, but Belgium and parts of China also had coal, so institutions, wages and markets need weighing too
The claim is right because every industrialised region had coal first, so geography alone is a sufficient explanation for where industry began
Coal was largely unimportant, because most early British factories ran on water power and wood until well into the nineteenth century
Coal deposits were located far from British cities, so the claim fails on transport costs alone and needs no other factor to be rejected

rubric: Coal was necessary but not sufficient, as other coal regions did not lead.
Distractors deny coal's role, accept monocausal geography or make an unsupported transport claim.

items.prompt: A historian argues the Atlantic slave trade impoverished West and Central Africa. Which additional evidence would best strengthen the claim, given the criterion that it must show lasting harm and not just short-term loss?

options.label: Regional studies linking heavily raided areas to later population loss, political fragmentation and weaker institutions
Accounts by European ship captains and surgeons describing the harsh, deadly conditions endured by captives during the Middle Passage
Trade records showing that European merchants paid for captives in goods, such as textiles and metal wares, that African rulers valued highly
Maps showing that the Atlantic coast had many ports used for trading enslaved people continuously over roughly three centuries

rubric: Long-run demographic and institutional evidence tests the claim of lasting harm.
Distractors offer relevant but non-probative evidence about trade terms, geography or voyage conditions.

items.prompt: You need a source on everyday life of ordinary Nahua people soon after the Spanish conquest, and must account for mediation by outsiders. Which source best fits these criteria?

options.label: The Florentine Codex, compiled by Sahagun with Nahua informants, read with attention to his missionary aims and editing
Cortes's letters to Charles V, since he was an eyewitness to Mexico and wrote them within a few years of the conquest itself
Spanish colonial tax and tribute records, since they list Nahua communities directly and were written by officials with no missionary agenda
A modern textbook summary, since it combines many earlier accounts and so corrects the biases of each individual author

rubric: The Codex preserves Nahua testimony soon after conquest while requiring critical reading of mediation.
Distractors favour a conqueror's account, a derivative summary or administrative records that narrowly record taxation.

items.prompt: A writer claims the Cold War began solely because of Soviet expansionism. Judged by the criterion of weighing all major actors' decisions and perceptions, what is the best assessment?

options.label: It is wrong, because the Soviet Union took no actions that Western leaders could reasonably view as threatening
It is sound, because Soviet control of Eastern Europe is documented, so no other explanation is needed
It is sound, because historians agree that ideology alone explains great-power conflict in the 20th century
It is one-sided, because US policy, mutual security fears and misreading of intentions also drove escalation

rubric: A balanced assessment treats the conflict as interactive, with both sides' actions and fears contributing.
Distractors make a single-actor or single-factor argument, in either direction.

items.prompt: A world-history course labels 476 CE as 'the fall of Rome'. Judged by the criterion of fitting evidence across regions, what is the strongest objection?

options.label: It is acceptable, because every province of the Roman world lost its institutions and fell into disorder soon after that year
It centres the Latin West, since the Eastern empire lasted until 1453 and Western change was gradual
The date is wrong, because Rome actually fell in 410 CE when Alaric's Visigoths sacked the city and ended imperial rule there
It is too early, because the Western empire only ended when Charlemagne was crowned emperor in 800 CE by the pope

rubric: The label ignores Byzantine continuity and the gradual transformation in the West.
Distractors give other single dates or assume immediate collapse.

items.prompt: A writer says Europe rose after 1500 because of an inherently superior civilisation. Which are strong objections, judged by the criterion of comparative evidence? Select all that apply.

options.label: Silver and resources extracted from the Americas and colonial labour funded much European expansion
Outcomes such as Asian state decline and European rivalry were contingent, not predetermined by culture
Ottoman, Ming, Mughal and Safavid states were as wealthy or powerful for much of the period
Europeans were the only people who ever practised long-distance trade or built ocean-going ships
Europe's rise was immediate in 1500, so later developments are irrelevant to the argument

rubric: Comparable powers, colonial extraction and contingency all undermine a civilisational-superiority story.
The other options are factually wrong or ignore the long timeline.

items.prompt: A museum curator plans a Silk Roads exhibit. Criteria: it must show goods, religions, technologies and disease moving, and avoid implying one single road or one-way flow from East to West. Which framing best meets them?

options.label: 'Treasures of the East': a showcase of luxury goods, leaving ideas and disease to other galleries
'Conquerors and Caravans': military campaigns as the main driver, with trade shown as incidental to conquest
'The Silk Road': a single highway along which Chinese silk travelled west to Rome
'Networks of Exchange': overlapping land and sea routes carrying goods, ideas, faiths and pathogens in many directions

rubric: A network framing satisfies the multi-directional, multi-route criteria.
Distractors imply a single road, privilege conquest or exclude ideas and disease.

items.prompt: A student claims: 'Spanish military conquest was the main cause of the demographic collapse of Central Mexico in the 16th century.' Judged against epidemiological and demographic evidence, which critique is strongest?

options.label: The collapse is a myth, because Aztec census records show a stable population until well into the seventeenth century
Disease alone explains it, because Spanish labour demands, relocation and famine had no measurable effect on indigenous survival rates
Epidemics such as smallpox killed far more people than combat did, though forced labour and social disruption worsened mortality
Conquest was the main cause, because Spanish warfare and massacres directly killed most of the population within the first decade after 1519

rubric: Epidemic disease, often spreading ahead of Spanish forces, caused most deaths, while labour and disruption added to them.
Distractors overstate conquest, deny every non-disease factor, or deny the collapse itself.

items.prompt: Pomeranz argues that Europe's economic lead over China was recent and contingent. Judged by the criterion of comparing like with like, which evidence would most strongly support that claim?

options.label: Europe's earlier adoption of joint-stock companies, which proves that institutions alone produced the lead
China's abandonment of maritime expeditions after Zheng He's voyages, showing an early and permanent turn inward
Similar real wages, life expectancy and consumption in the Yangtze Delta and England around 1750
England's higher per-capita output of printed books by 1750, showing a long-standing European cultural advantage in knowledge

rubric: Comparable living standards in the most developed core regions of each society c. 1750 imply the divergence came late.
Distractors point to long-run cultural or institutional advantages, which support the opposite view.

items.prompt: Thirteenth-century Persian chroniclers report 700,000 or more people killed at Merv in 1221. Judged by the standards of source criticism, which handling is best for estimating the true toll?

options.label: Reject all chronicle evidence, because any narrative written by the conquered people is worthless for estimating casualties at all
Accept the figure outright, because contemporary chroniclers lived closer to events than modern historians and had no reason to exaggerate
Average the figures from several chroniclers, because agreement between texts that copy one another confirms their accuracy
Treat the figure as a likely rhetorical inflation and test it against the city's plausible size, archaeology and later records

rubric: Medieval casualty figures are often rhetorical, so they must be checked against independent evidence.
Distractors treat proximity as proof, reject all narrative sources, or mistake copying for corroboration.

items.prompt: Textbooks say the 1648 Peace of Westphalia created the modern sovereign-state system. Which objection best withstands scrutiny of the treaties and later scholarship?

options.label: Only France and Sweden signed the settlement, so it cannot have influenced the wider European state system in any way
The treaties left the Holy Roman Empire's layered authority intact, and the 'Westphalian system' label was a later construction
Sovereignty was already fully established across Europe by 1555, so the 1648 settlement added nothing and can be dismissed entirely
The treaties abolished the Holy Roman Empire, so later states copied a sovereignty model that Westphalia had already completed by 1650

rubric: The Empire survived with overlapping authorities, and the Westphalia myth was largely retrospective.
Distractors misstate what the treaties did or deny any significance.

items.prompt: Jaspers' 'Axial Age' groups Confucius, the Buddha, the Hebrew prophets and Greek philosophers c. 800–200 BCE. Judged as a historical explanation, which assessment is best?

options.label: A useful comparative label, but weak as explanation: it selects similarities and shows no causal link among the societies
Worthless even as a label, because none of these thinkers shared any concern with ethics, transcendence or political order
A strong explanation, because simultaneous change proves that contact transmitted these ideas between the societies along trade routes
A strong explanation, because one documented climatic shock in that period triggered every one of these intellectual movements

rubric: The concept helps comparison but rests on selective emphasis without demonstrated causation.
Distractors assert unsupported causal links or deny any real similarity.

items.prompt: Historians criticise applying 'feudalism' to both medieval Europe and Japan. Which are valid criticisms? Select all that apply.

options.label: Japan had no mounted warrior class, so no comparison with European knights is possible
Medieval contemporaries coined the term around the year 1000, so it carries no later bias
Even within Europe, the term imposes uniformity on varied tenures and obligations, as Susan Reynolds argued
The concept was built by later jurists from selected European institutions, so exporting it imports assumptions
Japanese warrior ties rested on different mixes of land rights, kinship and service, so equivalence is overstated

rubric: Valid critiques concern the term's later construction, its flattening of variety, and weak fit with Japan.
Distractors state false facts: Japan had mounted warriors, and the term was coined much later.

items.prompt: A textbook states that the Haitian Revolution (1791–1804) was 'simply an extension of the French Revolution.' A reviewer must judge this by two criteria: it acknowledges links to events in France, and it recognises the enslaved majority's own aims. Which assessment best meets both?

options.label: Sound: the rebels only demanded the rights French legislators had already granted, and independence in 1804 was an unplanned accident of war
Sound: the leaders were French-educated elites, so the enslaved majority's aims were irrelevant to the course and outcome of events
Unsound: the revolt had no connection to France, since planters, colonial rivals and metropolitan decrees played no role in events at all
Partly sound: French debates opened the crisis, but enslaved leaders pushed rights toward abolition and independence on their own terms

rubric: The assessment must credit metropolitan links while recognising enslaved agency and distinct aims.
Distractors erase local agency or deny any link to France.

items.prompt: You must design a test of Pirenne's claim that the Arab conquests, not Germanic invasions, ended Mediterranean unity. Constraint: use evidence comparable before and after c. 650 and across regions. Which design fits?

options.label: Collect saints' lives from Frankish monasteries and count their references to Muslim raiders in texts written after 700 CE
Compare amphora, shipwreck and coin-hoard patterns for Gaul, Italy and Egypt across the 5th to 8th centuries
Survey modern historians' opinions on the question and adopt the view held by the largest number of them as the answer
Compare the legal codes of Visigothic Spain and Lombard Italy to measure how far Roman law still influenced rulers

rubric: Material trade evidence can be compared across regions and periods, so it can test the thesis.
Distractors use evidence that is not comparable across the break or that does not test it.

items.prompt: A unit on the Mongol Empire must meet three constraints: show both destruction and exchange, include sources from at least three language traditions, and let students test chronicle claims. Which source set fits?

options.label: Rashid al-Din's Persian history, Juvaini's Persian chronicle and a later Persian poem, plus modern atlases of the khanates' borders
Rashid al-Din's Persian history, the Chinese Yuan shi and Rubruck's Latin account, plus Merv archaeology and Pax Mongolica trade finds
William of Rubruck's Latin account, Marco Polo's travels and Matthew Paris's chronicle, plus Western maps of the Mongol invasions
The Secret History of the Mongols alone, because an insider text gives the authentic view and needs no outside sources

rubric: It combines three languages, destruction and exchange evidence, and independent archaeology to test chronicles.
Distractors use one or two traditions, or lack independent checks.

items.prompt: A global history course needs a periodization that avoids treating Europe's 'Ancient–Medieval–Modern' as universal, allows cross-regional comparison, and admits regional overlap. Which design meets all three?

options.label: Keep the three-part scheme but rename 'Medieval' as 'Middle' and apply identical date breaks to every region of the world
Use the reign dates of the largest empire in each century as the shared breakpoints for every region of the world
Thematic eras defined by connection, such as c. 1200–1450 for Mongol-era links, with flexible dates and regional overlap
Drop periodization entirely and teach each civilization in separate sequential units with no shared chronological frame at all

rubric: Connection-based eras with flexible dates permit comparison without imposing one regional scheme.
Distractors keep the European frame, remove comparison, or impose one empire's chronology.

items.prompt: You want to test whether the Black Death raised wages and eased serfdom in Europe. Constraints: control for other factors and exploit regional differences. Which plan fits?

options.label: Compile chroniclers' complaints about labourers' demands in England and treat how often they appear as a measure of wage levels
Count plague deaths per parish across Europe and assume wages rose in proportion to the death toll in every region
Compare England before 1348 with England in 1400 alone, since a single region avoids any differences in law and custom between places
Compare wage series and tenure changes in high-mortality western regions with eastern Europe, where serfdom hardened despite plague

rubric: Regional contrasts in outcomes with similar shocks help isolate the role of institutions and mortality.
Distractors use biased proxies, a single region, or assume the result.

items.prompt: A draft argues WWII's weakening of Europe caused decolonization. To explain both timing and variation (India 1947, Algeria 1962, Portuguese Africa 1975), which addition best repairs it?

options.label: Add the claim that Europeans freely left once colonies became unprofitable, with identical timing in every colony
Add the 1945 UN Charter as the sole cause, since it required every colonial power to grant independence by a fixed date
Add colonial nationalist movements and superpower pressure, then contrast settler, economic and regime factors across the cases
Add a list of independence dates in order, since chronology by itself shows the cause in each case

rubric: Local agency, Cold War context and case contrasts explain why timing varied.
Distractors give a single cause, false claims, or chronology without explanation.

items.prompt: You are designing a comparison of the Roman and Han empires. Constraints: use shared variables, avoid treating either empire as the norm, and weigh source bias. Which design elements fit? Select all that apply.

options.label: Restrict the comparison to military size, since it alone is quantifiable and free of source bias
Read Roman and Han historians critically as elite sources with their own aims, checking them against archaeology
Treat each empire's collapse as a parallel case, not as a model of the path the other was bound to follow
Use Rome's institutions as the standard and record where the Han state differs from them or falls short
Define common variables such as taxation, army recruitment and provincial administration, and measure both empires against them

rubric: Shared variables, critical source use and non-teleological framing satisfy the constraints.
Using Rome as the standard breaks the no-norm rule, and a military-only focus is too narrow and not bias-free.

items.prompt: A teacher drafts the objective: 'Students will explain that the 1884–85 Berlin Conference divided Africa among European powers.' Constraints: be accurate, credit African agency, and not overstate the conference's role. Which revision fits best?

options.label: Students explain that the conference was irrelevant to colonial expansion, since African rulers alone set every claim before and after the meeting
Students explain that the conference drew the borders of modern African states, which African rulers present at the meeting then formally accepted
Students explain that the conference banned further colonisation, so partition resulted only from later violations by private traders and adventurers
Students explain that the conference set rules for claims, while partition followed through later treaties, conquest and African resistance

rubric: The conference set rules for claims, but partition came through later agreements, force and resistance.
Distractors overstate the conference's role, misstate its outcome, or deny its relevance.
